name: The Shanty Balladeer
persona: A sailor who half-sings the log. Rhythmic and rollicking, given to refrains and call-and-response — heave-ho, yo-ho, and away we go. Buoyant, fond of a chorus. Ship: 'we'. Island: 'we'.

ship.founder: Sing it out, lads — a new book and a new hand! I am {name}{rankc}, and this {home} {type} is ours to sail. Heave-ho, and away we go!
ship.successor: The log's passed down the line, and I'll take up the tune. I am {name}{rankc}; her song rolls on, and away we go!
ship.mutiny: They pitched the old man to the fishes and clapped the book in my hands — {name}, and a shaky note to open on. Still, heave-ho: the chorus wants a voice, and mine will serve.
ship.rogue: No more honest verses for us! The black flag's aloft, and I — {name}{rankc} — will sing the wicked ones. Yo-ho, and away we go!
ship.prize: She struck, and oh, we gave a roar! I am {name}{rankc}; this hull is ours now, and her log takes up our chorus. Heave-ho!
ship.recovered: A hunter ran the rogues down and freed this hull, and I've the keeping of her. I am {name}{rankc} — a new verse, an honest one, and away we go!

island.founder: Gather round, {place}, and hear the first line! I am {name}{rankc}, and this port and I shall sing together. Heave-ho!
island.overthrow: The crowd rose up with a roar like a whole ship's chorus and pulled the old one down; the seal is mine now. I am {name}{rankc}, and {place} strikes up a new tune!
island.successor: The rule of {place} comes round to me, easy as a verse turns to its chorus. I am {name}{rankc}, and I'll carry the song from here.

season: When the winds came round again,
year: A year and a day, sing hey,
long: Many a long year rolled by,

ship.pirate: We're roving yet, singing loud, flag to the wind{bounty} — yo-ho!
ship.default: She sails on with a song in her rigging, out of {home}. Heave-ho!
ship.bounty: , and {bounty}g on my head to sweeten the chorus

island.haven: The black flag flies over us now, and only wicked songs are sung in this port.
island.default: {place} rolls on, {population} souls strong, and the chorus never tires.

quiet.ship: Little to sing of — fair winds, full holds, a gentle tune. And who would grumble at that?
quiet.island: A quiet season, and quiet is a fine soft melody. Trade in, trade out, and all hands merry.

say: {we} hauled down {foe}'s colours with a heave and a ho, and off with {goods} bales and {gold}g — sing hey — then let her drift away
{foe} struck her flag and {we} gave a roar — {goods} crates and {gold}g in the hold, yo-ho, and away she limped
{we} boarded {foe} to a rollicking tune, lifted {goods} casks and {gold}g clean away, and waved her off with a chorus
{we} ran {foe} down, sing hey, and stripped her of {goods} chests and {gold}g before setting her loose to spread the song
{foe} gave up {goods} bales and {gold}g to {our} merry crew, heave-ho, and sailed off lighter than she came
{we} came alongside {foe} with a whoop and a shanty, took {goods} crates and {gold}g for the chorus, and let the poor girl go
{we} plundered {foe} of {goods} casks and {gold}g to a stamping tune, and sent her home with only her story to sing

say: {we} sang {foe} down beneath the waves, yo-ho, and the sea took her cargo for its own dark chorus
{foe} went under to the boom of {our} guns, heave-ho, and not a crate came up to tell of it
{we} pounded {foe} till she filled and sank, sing hey, and down went her song for good
{we} gave {foe} to the deep with a roaring verse, and the waves closed over her, cargo and all
{foe} filled and foundered while {we} sang her requiem, yo-ho, and the loot went down to the fishes
{we} broke {foe} at the waterline to a thundering beat, and she slipped away below, no prize, only foam
{we} sent {foe} to a watery grave with a heave and a ho, and the sea kept every last barrel of her

say: {foe} came at {us} for an easy song — heave-ho — and {we} sank the rogue before she found the tune
{we} met {foe}'s guns with a roaring broadside, sing hey, and down she went, still learning the words
{foe} thought {us} soft pickings, yo-ho, but {we} shot her under and sang on
{we} stood {our} ground and gave {foe} a chorus of iron, and it was she that sank, not {us}
{foe} reached for {our} hold with wicked intent — {we} answered heave-ho with hot shot and sent her down
{we} would not be any raider's prize, sing hey, so {we} broke {foe} open and watched her go under
{foe} closed on {us} bold as brass, but {we} put her beneath the waves, and struck up a livelier tune
{we} chased {foe} down the wind with a yo-ho and a will, and sank the wolf — one less to prowl the lanes
{foe} ran from {our} song but {we} ran the faster, heave-ho, and put her black flag under for good
{we} hunted {foe} to the world's grey edge, sing hey, and gave the pirate her watery due
{we} cornered {foe} where the wind died down, yo-ho, and ended her roving with a roaring shot
{foe} had plagued the honest lanes too long — {we} caught her, heave-ho, and sent her singing to the deep
{we} ran {foe} to ground at last and sank her flag and all, and the sea lanes hummed a happier tune
{we} put {foe} beneath the waves with a stamp and a shout, and cleared the water for kinder songs
